name: United Kingdom

territory.border: hb:1815:United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

areaKm2.note: world_1815 polygon "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland" = 288,100 km2 on the sphere; Great Britain ~229,000 + Ireland ~84,000 = ~314,000 km2. The 1815 file also has a "United Kingdom" feature that is only the Caribbean colonies.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1816 = 19,520k (UK of Great Britain and Ireland). 1815 taken slightly lower. GB 1811 census ~12.6M civilians plus Ireland ~6M.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share, United Kingdom (modern borders, mostly GB): 32.1% (1810), 35.4% (1820) = high end. Ireland ~7-8% urban pulls the UK-with-Ireland figure down; towns of 5,000+ in England ~25-30%.

activePersonnel.note: Regular army peaked at over 250,000 in 1813 (page); by June 1815 ~220,000-230,000 after the 1814 reductions and Hundred Days re-expansion, plus Ordnance corps (Royal Artillery, engineers) ~25,000 and Royal Navy with marines ~100,000-140,000. COW NMC v7 milper 1816 = 255,000 after demobilisation had begun. East India Company armies (~200,000, mostly sepoys) excluded.

trainedReserves.note: Militia (ballot-raised, embodiable), local militia and yeomanry. Volunteers reached ~329,000 in 1806 (page) but were largely disbanded by 1814-15; the regular militia was partly disembodied in 1814. Range spans 1815 militia plus surviving local forces.

supportPersonnel.note: Royal Navy seamen and Royal Marines ~100,000 in mid-1815 (down from ~140,000 voted in 1813-14), Royal Artillery and Royal Engineers ~22,000, commissariat, staff and drivers ~8,000. Reconstruction from the British Army page and Rodger (isbn:978-0-14-102690-9, ch. on 1815 manning).

mobilizationRatio.note: Peak 1809-1813: regular army ~250,000 (British Army page) + navy ~140,000 + militia ~100,000 + local militia/volunteers ~300,000 = ~790,000 of ~18M = 4.4%. Voluntary enlistment, no conscription for the regulars.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Line and Guards battalions incl. the King's German Legion. Whole infantry was 126,677 in 1803 (page); 1813-15 peak army >250,000 with roughly 60% infantry. Includes colonial garrisons (West Indies, Canada, Gibraltar, Malta, Cape, Ceylon).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Brown Bess India pattern musket, era-standard; superior musketry practice

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: long-service volunteers, Peninsular veterans; many second battalions and 1815 units green

count.note: 95th Rifles (3 bns), KGL light battalions and the light infantry regiments (43rd, 51st, 52nd, 68th, 71st, 85th) ~1,000 each; flank companies stay in line. Reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Baker rifle in the 95th, the best skirmish weapon of the era

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Shorncliffe light-infantry system, Light Division record

count.note: Household Cavalry (3 regts), Dragoon Guards (7) and heavy Dragoons (6) at ~500-650 present.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: big horses, 1796 heavy sword; no cuirass outside the Household

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: brave but poorly controlled in the charge (Union Brigade at Waterloo)

count.note: Light Dragoons and Hussars (~20 regts) at ~500-650 present; dragoons of the light pattern counted here.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: good horses, 1796 light cavalry sabre

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: outpost work weaker than the KGL hussars

count.note: Field guns of RA foot brigades and RHA troops in service across all theatres. Waterloo campaign Anglo-allied army ~150 guns (page gives Wellington 107,000 men); British share ~100. Fortress and coast guns excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: 9-pdrs, Shrapnel spherical case shot (unique to Britain), Congreve rockets

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: RHA the equal of the French horse artillery

count.note: Ships of the line in commission, mid-1815. Rodger, Command of the Ocean (2004) app.: ~100 of the line in sea service at the 1813-14 peak, many paid off after April 1814 and only partly recommissioned in the Hundred Days; frigates counted as minor, as in france-1805. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: 74s and three-deckers, coppered hulls, carronades

training.note: Rubric row: training 1.0. Evidence: two decades of sea-keeping and gunnery; Trafalgar and blockade record

count.note: Frigates, sloops, brigs and cutters in commission 1814-15 (Rodger appendix: ~600 vessels of all classes at the peak, reduced in 1814-15). audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: large frigate force; the US 44s outgunned single British frigates in 1812

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: professional crews, impressment notwithstanding

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75. Evidence: Wellington (Peninsula 1808-14, Waterloo), but a thin staff and a Horse Guards / Ordnance split

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75-1.0. Evidence: regimental system, long-service volunteers held squares at Waterloo

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75. Evidence: Peninsular victories 1812-14, Napoleon's return opposed by a coalition

weapons.note: Anchor: 6 (1805). Evidence: Brown Bess, Baker rifle, Shrapnel shell and Congreve rockets slightly ahead of the 1805 anchor

armor.note: Anchor: 6 (none / cuirass). Evidence: no cuirassiers outside the Household Cavalry

ships.note: Anchor: 6 (74-gun ships of the line). Evidence: the largest coppered battle fleet; still all sail audit 2026-10-30: mid 6.2 -> 6.1, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1815 (6.100); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

fortification.note: Anchor: 6 (Vauban-type forts). Evidence: Gibraltar, Portsmouth and Plymouth lines, Martello towers

logistics.note: Anchor: 6 (magazines + requisition). Evidence: commissariat paid for supplies and sea lift kept Wellington supplied in Iberia audit 2026-10-30: mid 6.2 -> 6.1, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1815 (6.100); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

communications.note: Anchor: 6 (semaphore telegraph). Evidence: Admiralty shutter telegraph London-Deal/Portsmouth/Plymouth

isr.note: Anchor: 6 (1805). Evidence: exploring officers, naval scouting, captured correspondence

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID), United Kingdom 1815 = 3,489 (2011 int$), a Great Britain-weighted series. Ireland was much poorer (roughly half), so the UK-with-Ireland mean is put near 2,950; high = the GB value.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: at war in June 1815; army, navy and ordnance took ~£60-70M of ~£110M public spending at the 1814 peak against a national income of ~£350-400M. Low = 1790s peacetime share; COW milex 1816 = £16.9M (post-war).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: Deane and Cole style national accounts put manufacturing, mining and building near 30% of British income around 1811-1821; Ireland lowers the UK share.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). a: Herrendorf et al. via OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/employment-by-economic-sector.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true), United Kingdom agriculture share of employment 1801 = 30.8%, 1841 = 21.1%, interpolated ~27% for 1815 ("about a third" for Britain). The snapshot includes Ireland (~6M of 19.3M), more agrarian; ~0.65 assumed for it (not fetched), giving a ~0.39. s = 1 assumed: grain imports small, Ireland exported food. Mid 1 - 0.39 = 0.61; low a 0.45; high 0.73 if the OWID series already includes Ireland. Grade D. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.3/0.4/0.5, which contradicted the note's own farm share; recomputed with the formula.

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: ships of the line launched or captured per year 1803-1815 in Royal and merchant yards.

artillery.note: Educated guess: field-gun output of the Woolwich foundry and contractors (Carron, Walker) per year; naval guns far more numerous.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: turnpike trusts managed ~20,000 miles (~32,000 km) of improved road in Britain by the 1820s; Irish mail roads added.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: London, Liverpool, Bristol, Glasgow, Hull, Leith, Newcastle, Portsmouth, Plymouth, Chatham, Cork, Dublin.

merchantTonnage.note: Registered merchant tonnage 2,323k tons (United Kingdom 1815, CHAT dataset https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta, variable shipton_all) x 1.5 (range 1.3-1.6). CHAT tonnage is registered (largely net) tons, so this may understate deadweight.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: Peninsular armies operated 150-400 km from sea depots with mule trains; Britain's reach is by sea.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: roughly 1.2-1.5M horses in Britain plus Irish horses and oxen.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified dockyards and population support; insular, no harsh-climate depth.

notes: Snapshot = United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland in June 1815 (Hundred Days, Waterloo campaign). Population and territory = Great Britain and Ireland; colonies and the East India Company (its presidency armies of ~200,000) are excluded and includes is empty. Personnel: regular army, Ordnance corps and navy = active; militia, local militia and yeomanry = trainedReserves. Waterloo campaign: Wellington 107,000 (Anglo-allied, of whom ~31,000 British), Bluecher 123,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterloo_campaign). COW data start in 1816, so 1816 values are used as anchors. Branch counts are reconstructions, grade C. Frigates are counted as ships_minor to match france-1805.
